skill.name: w-council
skill.description: Inspect a requested codebase area with parallel explorers, reconcile their reports against the tree, and hand off findings or an implementation plan.
skill.summary: Coordinate focused codebase investigations with parallel explorers and evidence-based handoffs.
skill.author: blockmatic

content.value_statement: Codebase investigations can miss important context when one review follows a single path. This skill coordinates focused explorers, reconciles their evidence, and produces a clear handoff.
actual_capabilities: Inspects the requested code area before delegating work.
Records architecture details and search keywords for investigators.
Spawns two or three explorers with distinct investigation angles.
Reconciles agent reports against current files and working tree changes.
Hands off findings, assumptions, references, and deferred work.
limitations: It investigates and plans but does not implement changes.
It does not commit, push, or open pull requests.
Investigation quality depends on the requested scope and available repository evidence.
It does not replace tests, code review, or security validation.

use_cases.title: Map an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Ask the skill to identify owning packages, current behavior, and relevant architecture before a larger engineering task.

use_cases.title: Investigate a focused bug area
use_cases.description: Use parallel explorers to examine a suspected subsystem from implementation, history, and edge-case perspectives.

use_cases.title: Prepare an implementation handoff
use_cases.description: Request an evidence-based plan with references, assumptions, and explicit deferrals for another agent or teammate.

prompt_templates.title: Start a repository investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use w-council to inspect the authentication area. Summarize its owning packages, current behavior, and the files that matter most.

prompt_templates.title: Compare investigation angles
prompt_templates.prompt: Use w-council to investigate the cache invalidation issue with separate explorers for implementation flow, tests, and unusual edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Validate findings against the tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Use w-council to investigate the deployment pipeline. Reconcile every report against the current tree and identify findings that lack file evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a constrained handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use w-council to investigate the proposed API change, then provide references, three to five assumptions, deferred questions, and an implementation-ready handoff without editing files.

output_examples.input: Investigate how session expiration works in this repository.
output_examples.output: The session flow is owned by the authentication package. Reports identify the token parser, refresh handler, and expiration tests as the key evidence.

output_examples.input: Explore the build pipeline before I ask for a change.
output: Architecture: the pipeline begins with repository configuration and delegates packaging to the release workflow.
Evidence: the current behavior is supported by the workflow definitions and their related tests.
Handoff: implementation should begin by confirming the release trigger and preserving existing artifact checks.

best_practices: Give the investigation a specific area, behavior, or question.
Ask explorers to use distinct angles with bounded scopes.
Require every important conclusion to include file evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not request implementation when you only need an investigation.
Do not accept agent summaries without checking the current tree.
Do not split a small question into unnecessary parallel runs.

faq.question: What does w-council do?
faq.answer: It coordinates a small group of codebase explorers, then reconciles their reports into an evidence-based handoff.

faq.question: Does it edit repository files?
faq.answer: No. It inspects and plans. Implementation requires a separate request and the appropriate build workflow.

faq.question: How many explorers does it use?
faq.answer: It defaults to two or three explorers and adjusts the count to the investigation scope.

faq.question: Can it investigate changing working trees?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for re-verification when the working tree changes during the investigation.

faq.question: What should a handoff include?
faq.answer: A useful handoff includes evidence, references, assumptions, unresolved questions, and deferred work.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It improves discovery and planning, but tests, implementation review, and security validation remain necessary.
